statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month last traded near 29,565.25, up 0.14%, mid-range inside a Sunday restart band of 29,530.50-29,622.75 that has now contained roughly six hours of trade. The marginal new high tagged late in the previous hour was given back in full. Stress holds at 55 on a ten-year yield near 4.784%, a 58% market-implied probability of a Federal Reserve hike on 16 September, WTI near $92.43 after a weekly gain close to 10%, and an Iranian restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz that Tehran has signalled but not yet declared.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk concentrates in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the early Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook. headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 92-point Sunday restart range for a sixth hour while Asia splits between a 2.2% Nikkei rally and a Hang Seng decline of more than 1%
body:
The defining observation of this hour is containment. NQ front-month last printed 29,565.25, up 40.50 points or 0.14%, inside a restart range of 29,530.50 to 29,622.75. That band is roughly 92 points or 0.31% wide and has now held for about six hours. The marginal new high near 29,622.75 tagged late in the previous hour was returned in full, and price sits close to the middle of the range rather than pressing either extreme. Repeated extension after failed retracements, shallow pullbacks and holding near session extremes are the structures that overwhelm a reverse or mean-reversion strategy, and none of the three is present. That is why Tail stays at the low-band floor rather than carrying a thin-book premium.

The regional picture became more divided rather than more aligned. Reuters reports Japan's Nikkei up 2.2% and South Korea up 3.1%, both led by chipmakers on AI demand, with Chinese blue chips adding only 0.2% and MSCI's Asia-Pacific-ex-Japan index up 1.1%. Against that, the Hang Seng is down more than 1% and the Hang Seng Tech index around 1.1% lower. A regional technology complex that rallies 3% in Seoul and falls 1% in Hong Kong within the same session is rotating, not trending, and NQ has tracked neither leg. Reuters characterised S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures as slightly lower over the same window, which is consistent with an index that is being pulled in both directions and settling in the middle.

Energy remains the live but chronic channel. WTI trades near $92.43 and Brent near $97.22, each about 1% higher on the day, after a week in which WTI gained close to 10% and Brent 7.8%. U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend, destroying one, in retaliation for ballistic-missile attacks on U.S. Navy warships, and Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary said on Sunday that a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz would be declared in the coming days alongside a new Oman-agreed shipping route. Kpler data show an average of ten commodity ships transiting the strait per day over the past ten days, the lowest since May. Seven OPEC+ producers left October quotas unchanged at a virtual meeting on 6 September. This is a severe but progressively priced supply disruption, and under the standing calibration a chronic and already-absorbed channel supports Stress rather than Tail.

The rate and volatility backdrop offers no amplifier. Ten-year Treasury yields sit near 4.7840%, close to their highest since late 2023, and markets price a 58% probability of a Federal Reserve hike at the 16 September meeting and 70% by October following Friday's upbeat payrolls report. The H.15 release still shows the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% as of 3 September. Gold has slipped toward $4,400 an ounce on the same hike repricing, and the dollar index sits at 99.135. Friday's VIX close of 14.53 is low in absolute terms and leaves no volatility premium to unwind. Friday's Nasdaq internals were split rather than aligned: the semiconductor complex closed uniformly higher, led by Micron and AMD, while five of eight megacaps fell and Tesla dropped almost 6%, and application software fell while semiconductor equipment gained nearly 5%. No cross-asset alignment of the kind that amplifies Tail is present.

Today is Labor Day. U.S. cash equity and Treasury markets are closed. CME Globex opened normally on Sunday evening but equity-index futures move to a pre-open state at 17:00 UTC, in which orders may be entered, modified or cancelled but not matched, and reopen at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. No settlement price is derived or disseminated for Monday. The narrow danger window therefore stays at 15:00 to 17:00 UTC, covering the European cash close into that hard deadline, because a squeeze into a fixed halt in an already thin book remains the most plausible unrepaired-move mechanism in this outlook. It is a conditional scenario, not an observation.

The week is back-loaded and today is empty. August PPI and initial jobless claims arrive on Thursday 10 September, and August CPI on Friday 11 September, the last inflation reading before the 15-16 September FOMC decision, with the Fed already in its pre-meeting communications blackout. None of those events falls inside this 24-hour outlook, and under the standing calibration event importance and forecast dispersion of that kind inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail.

Shared delayed cross-asset context was collected at 01:20 UTC and is now roughly three hours old, past its freshness threshold, so this assessment rests on independently verified live sources. Where the two overlap they agree: a flat index-futures complex, Treasury futures moving only a few basis points, a marginally softer VIX future and firmer crude.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, then eased to 6 and back to 5 once the restart proved orderly and stayed at 5 for the last five available hours. Stress ran from 55 down to a 52 low at 07:00 UTC, drifted up through a 54-58 band as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, peaked at 60 at 20:00 UTC, then eased to 57, 56, 55, 54, 54 and 55 after the reopen. Confidence held a narrow 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the Asian session, a European session traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that moves to pre-open at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 through the remaining Asian hours while the restart range holds, 6 across the Asian-to-European handover, 7 from the European cash open through mid-morning where the weekend Iran and Hormuz headlines first meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 6 through the holiday-thinned midday, 7 across the notional US open and early afternoon, 8 as the danger window opens at the European cash close and 8 in the final hour before the halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are shut, then 8 at the Tuesday restart easing to 7, 6 and 5. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape between 53 and 58, and Confidence decays from 86 to 71 as the assessment ages away from its evidence cutoff.
